FLASHCARD SET · AGES 3–4 YEARS

Alphabet Flashcards A–Z

Twenty-six picture cards, one for every letter from A to Z. Big letters, little letters, familiar things to name — pick a card, say it together and stop whenever your preschooler has had enough.

THE ALPHABET CENTER

Meet the alphabet, one card at a time.

Twenty-six letters, five kinds of cards and every picture from the school’s alphabet set. Choose a card kind below, move through the alphabet with the arrows, shuffle for surprise practice — or tap any letter in the big grid to jump straight to it.

Uppercase, lowercase, picture, pair and letter-&-picture cards — one kind at a time, big and touch-friendly. Nothing here is scored or timed.

HOW TO USE THESE CARDS

Four ways that work.

You do not need a plan or a printer schedule. Pick one idea, try it for two minutes and see what happens.

  1. 01

    Three cards is a lovely day

    Pick a few, look at them slowly and stop while it is still fun. You do not need to finish the alphabet in one sitting — or even in one week.

  2. 02

    Start with your child’s own letter

    The first letter of your child’s name is the most interesting letter in the world to them. Begin there and watch how proudly they find it.

  3. 03

    Say the sound, not just the name

    The letter is named A, but it says a — like the very start of apple. Say both, casually, and let your child copy whichever one they like.

  4. 04

    Give today’s card a home

    Tape the card of the day to the fridge or a bedroom door at your child’s eye level. Passing it again and again is quietly powerful practice.
